data.name: Ashraqat
data.gender_notes: Ashraqat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'ash-sharqu', meaning 'east'. Ashraqat symbolizes the beautiful and radiant light of the moon during an eastward journey, which is a metaphor for a prosperous and enlightened life in Islam. The name Ashraqat carries the meaning “Moonlit night” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ashraqat usually hope their child will grow to embody moonlit night and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine guidance and protection, Ashraqat represents the light of the Quran illuminating one's path and the blessings of Allah SWT.
data.etymology: Ashraqat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moonlit night.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashraqat total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.
